podcast.body: Released in 1969, this song initially snuck into the Hot 100 at number 91 before creeping into the top 10. Described as "assertive and loud and... kind of sexy," its sound and Robert Plant's "pre-a-pick" stage performance with the microphone stand contributed to the beginning of heavy metal. Despite its significance, some 1970 reviewers found it "pure nonsense, painful to listen to" and only tolerable for Jimmy Page's guitar riffs. "Whole lot of love in 1969 was pre-a-pick."

The lyrics to this major 1969 song were found to be too close to Willie Dixon's 1962 song "You Need Love." It wasn't until 1985 that Dixon received a co-writing credit for the track. "And the lyrics to Whole Lot of Love, Big Song from 1969, were way too close to a 1962 Willie Dixon song entitled You Need Love."
